newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Officials accused of hindering new Vietnam courts.
newsitem.headline: Officials accused of hindering new Vietnam courts.

text.p: An official Vietnamese daily said on Wednesday that officials and vested interests were blocking a new court system aimed at allowing the public to sue government bodies.
The official Vietnam News said, with unusual candour, that of the thousands of cases put forward since the administrative court system was established last year only 100 had been heard.
"In many cases, the head of the administrative organs against whom the law suit was brought refused to give testimony," it said.
"In other cases, administrative courts refused to try a case for fear of causing friction with the defendant -- usually the local People's Committee (local government)."
The report said the new courts, established nationwide from July 1 last year, were too weak to take on government officials and needed to be reorganised.
Court officials and members of the Vietnam Bar Association declined comment on Wednesday and it was not immediately possible to verify the newspaper's claims.
Most public grievances with local authorities in Vietnam are reported to concern the sensitive issue of land-use rights.
Vietnam's communist government maintains that all land belongs to the state. Land can be claimed back from tenants in return for compensation rates decided by local authorities.

State newspapers reported last year that a top Hanoi People's Committee official had failed to turn up at a court hearing in which he was being sued over a decision to transfer ownership of a house. He later won the case.
